UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores profile information for a user within the FinWave application, linking all financial activities to a specific individual.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

firstName.description: The first name of the user.

lastName.description: The last name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user.

phoneNumber.description: The contact phone number of the user.

address.description: The physical address of the user.

dateJoined.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

Account.title: Account
Account.description: Represents a financial account held by a user, such as a checking or savings account, displaying balances and overall status.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Account entity.

accountNumber.description: The unique account number for this financial account.

accountName.description: A user-friendly name or alias for the account.

balance.description: The current monetary balance of the account.

currency.description: The currency code of the account's balance (e.g., 'USD', 'IDR').

isOpen.description: Indicates whether the account is currently active.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the account was created.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Records a single financial movement, including transfers, deposits, and withdrawals, associated with a specific account.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Transaction entity.

type.description: The type of transaction (e.g., 'Transfer Out', 'Transfer In', 'Deposit', 'Withdrawal', 'Bill Payment').

amount.description: The monetary amount of the transaction.

currency.description: The currency code of the transaction amount.

transactionDate.description: The date and time when the transaction occurred.

description.description: A brief description or memo for the transaction.

recipientName.description: The name of the recipient for outgoing transfers or payments.

recipientAccountNumber.description: The account number of the recipient for outgoing transfers or payments.

status.description: The current status of the transaction (e.g., 'Completed', 'Pending', 'Failed', 'Cancelled').

Beneficiary.title: Beneficiary
Beneficiary.description: Stores details of individuals or entities registered as recipients for fund transfers.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Beneficiary entity.

beneficiaryName.description: The full name or entity name of the beneficiary.

accountNumber.description: The account number of the beneficiary.

bankName.description: The name of the bank where the beneficiary's account is held.

bankCode.description: The SWIFT/BIC code or local bank code of the beneficiary's bank.

isVerified.description: Indicates if the beneficiary's details have been verified.

addedAt.description: Timestamp when the beneficiary was added by the user.

EWallet.title: EWallet
EWallet.description: Represents an external electronic wallet linked to the user's FinWave profile.

id.description: Unique identifier for the EWallet entity.

walletProvider.description: The name of the e-wallet service provider (e.g., 'Gopay', 'OVO').

walletIdentifier.description: The unique identifier for the user's e-wallet account (e.g., phone number, email).

balance.description: The current balance in the linked e-wallet, synchronized periodically.

currency.description: The currency code of the e-wallet balance.

linkedAt.description: Timestamp when the e-wallet was linked to the user's profile.

isLinked.description: Indicates if the e-wallet link is currently active.

DepositProduct.title: DepositProduct
DepositProduct.description: Defines the various deposit offerings or savings products available to users, such as fixed deposits or special savings plans.

id.description: Unique identifier for the DepositProduct entity.

productName.description: The official name of the deposit product offering.

description.description: A detailed description of the deposit product's features and terms.

interestRate.description: The annual interest rate offered by this deposit product (as a decimal, e.g., 0.05 for 5%).

minimumDepositAmount.description: The minimum principal amount required to open this deposit product.

currency.description: The currency code for the minimum deposit and interest calculations.

termLengthMonths.description: The fixed term length of the deposit product in months (if applicable).

isActive.description: Indicates if the deposit product is currently available for new deposits.

availableFrom.description: The date from which this product is available.

availableTo.description: The date until which this product is available (optional).

Deposit.title: Deposit
Deposit.description: Represents a specific deposit made by a user into one of the available deposit products.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Deposit entity.

accountId.description: Reference to Account. (Relationship: Account 1:N Deposit) The account from which funds were taken or to which earnings are paid.

currency.description: The currency code of the deposit amount.

startDate.description: The date when the deposit was initiated.

maturityDate.description: The date when the deposit matures (if fixed-term).

currentValue.description: The current value of the deposit, including accrued interest.

status.description: The current status of the deposit (e.g., 'Active', 'Matured', 'Early Withdrawal', 'Closed').

firestore.reasoning:
The FinWave Firestore structure is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence and adherence to Query As Authorization Predicates (QAPs), ensuring simple, robust, and easily debuggable security rules. All user-specific data is organized under a top-level `/users/{userId}` collection, making `request.auth.uid` the primary and most efficient authorization predicate.

**Authorization Independence:**

1.  **Path-Based Ownership:** For `UserProfile`, `Account`, `Beneficiary`, `EWallet`, and `Deposit` entities, the data is stored hierarchically under `/users/{userId}/...`. This directly embeds the user's unique ID (`userId`) into the document path. Consequently, security rules can evaluate `request.auth.uid == userId` immediately, without needing to perform any `get()` operations on parent documents. This completely eliminates hierarchical authorization dependencies, enabling atomic operations (transactions/batches) and significantly simplifying rule logic.
2.  **Denormalized User IDs:** For `Account`, `Beneficiary`, `EWallet`, and `Deposit` documents, the `userProfileId` field (referencing the owning user) is explicitly stored within each document. While the path itself provides the primary authorization context, this denormalization serves as a critical invariant and a robust secondary check within security rules (e.g., `resource.data.userProfileId == request.auth.uid`). This provides an additional layer of data integrity and self-contained authorization context for each document, reinforcing Authorization Independence.
3.  **Global Data Segregation:** `DepositProduct` entities are global, application-wide offerings. They are placed in a top-level `/depositProducts/{productId}` collection, completely separated from user-specific data. This structural segregation ensures that their access rules are homogeneous (e.g., all authenticated users can read, only admins can write) and do not depend on any user-specific context, further promoting Authorization Independence.

**Query As Authorization Predicates (QAPs):**

1.  **Implicit Scope for User Data:** By nesting all user-owned data under `/users/{userId}/`, any `list` operation initiated by an authenticated user (`request.auth.uid`) will naturally be scoped to their own data (e.g., `db.collection('users').doc(request.auth.uid).collection('accounts').get()`). Firestore security rules can then easily enforce that the `userId` in the path matches `request.auth.uid` for any read/write operation, guaranteeing that users can only query and access their own specific resources.
2.  **Explicit Public Scope:** The `/depositProducts` collection is designed for read-only access by all authenticated users. Security rules for this collection can simply allow `read` operations for `if request.auth != null`, ensuring that queries against this collection are secure and return only publicly available data, fulfilling QAPs for global datasets.

This design minimizes rule complexity, prevents common security pitfalls related to `get()` calls, and provides a highly predictable and debuggable authorization model suitable for a scalable financial application like FinWave.
